source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Exact source records mapped to established public labels; mapping is recorded for every verse and verified against source KJV annotations. Daniel, Hosea, Joel, Jonah, Micah, and Nahum have chapter-boundary differences.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Preserves origin, all three reigns, and both cities as vision scope.
verses.before: The word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to Micah of Moresheth during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah—what he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps universal summons, legal witness, and differing divine titles.
verses.before: Hear, all you peoples; give attention, O earth and all that fills it. And let the Lord GOD be witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.
verses.after: Hear, all you peoples! Listen, earth and everything in it! Let the Lord GOD be a witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear, all you peoples; give attention, O earth and all that fills it. And let the Lord GOD be witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.

verses.rationale: Preserves descent and high places as landscape with cultic resonance.
verses.before: For look, the LORD is coming out from his place. He will come down and tread upon the high places of the earth.
verses.after: Look, the LORD is coming out of his place. He will come down and tread the heights of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: For behold, the LORD is coming out from his place. He will come down and tread upon the high places of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps both terrain changes and two flowing/melting similes.
verses.before: The mountains will melt beneath him, and the valleys will split open, like wax before the fire, like waters poured down a steep place.
verses.after: The mountains will melt beneath him and the valleys split apart, like wax before fire, like water pouring down a slope.
verses.tsw_comparator: The mountains will melt beneath him, and the valleys will split open, like wax before the fire, like waters poured down a steep place.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult high-places clause and identification of each capital with wrongdoing.
verses.before: All this is because of the transgression of Jacob and because of the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what is the high place of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?
verses.after: All this is because of Jacob’s rebellion and the sins of the house of Israel. What is Jacob’s rebellion? Is it not Samaria? What are Judah’s high places? Are they not Jerusalem?
verses.tsw_comparator: All this is because of the transgression of Jacob and because of the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what is the high place of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?

verses.rationale: Preserves agricultural replacement, flowing stones, and exposed foundations.
verses.before: So I will make Samaria a heap in the open country, a place for planting vineyards. I will pour her stones into the valley and uncover her foundations.
verses.after: “I will make Samaria a heap in the open country, a place for planting vineyards. I will pour her stones into the valley and lay her foundations bare.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I will make Samaria a heap in the open country, a place for planting vineyards. I will pour her stones into the valley and uncover her foundations.

verses.rationale: Repeats wages to retain the accusation's circular economy without assuming a particular cult practice.
verses.before: All her carved images will be shattered, all her wages will be burned with fire, and all her idols I will make desolate. For from the wages of a prostitute she gathered them, and to the wages of a prostitute they will return.
verses.after: All her carved images will be smashed; all her prostitute’s wages burned with fire. I will devastate all her idols, for she gathered them from a prostitute’s wages, and to a prostitute’s wages they will return.”
verses.tsw_comparator: All her carved images shall be shattered, all her wages shall be burned with fire, and all her idols I will make desolate. For from the wages of a prostitute she gathered them, and to the wages of a prostitute they shall return.

verses.rationale: Keeps the prophet's exposed mourning and both animal cries, with species uncertainty noted if needed.
verses.before: Because of this I will lament and wail. I will go barefoot and naked. I will make a lament like the jackals and a mourning like the ostriches.
verses.after: Because of this I will lament and wail; I will go stripped and naked. I will lament like jackals and mourn like ostriches.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of this I will lament and wail. I will go barefoot and naked. I will make a lament like the jackals and a mourning like the ostriches.

verses.rationale: Makes the geographic progression clear while preserving the feminine wound image.
verses.before: For her wound is incurable, and it has come to Judah. It has reached to the gate of my people, to Jerusalem.
verses.after: Her wound is incurable. It has reached Judah; it has touched the gate of my people, Jerusalem itself.
verses.tsw_comparator: For her wound is incurable, and it has come to Judah. It has reached to the gate of my people, to Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Follows read feminine imperative rather than written I rolled; retains place/dust wordplay.
verses.before: Tell it not in Gath; weep not at all. At Beth-leaphrah roll yourselves in the dust.
verses.after: Do not tell it in Gath; do not weep at all. In Beth-leaphrah, roll yourself in dust.
verses.tsw_comparator: Tell it not in Gath; weep not at all. At Beth-leaphrah roll yourselves in the dust.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three difficult town puns and the obscure support clause without invented geography.
verses.before: Pass on your way, inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness and shame. The inhabitant of Zaanan does not come out. The lamentation of Beth-ezel takes away from you its standing place.
verses.after: Pass on, inhabitant of Shaphir, naked and shamed. The inhabitant of Zaanan has not come out. Beth-ezel’s mourning takes away its support from you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pass on your way, inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness and shame. The inhabitant of Zaanan does not come out. The lamentation of Beth-ezel takes away from you its standing place.

verses.rationale: Preserves bitter-town/good tension and explicit divine source of disaster.
verses.before: For the inhabitant of Maroth waits anxiously for good, because disaster has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.
verses.after: The inhabitant of Maroth writhes for good, for disaster has come down from the LORD to Jerusalem’s gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the inhabitant of Maroth waits anxiously for good, because disaster has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps horse/Lachish soundplay in note, personified daughter, and accusation without inventing historical details.
verses.before: Harness the chariot to the swift steeds, inhabitant of Lachish. She was the beginning of sin to the daughter of Zion, for in you were found the transgressions of Israel.
verses.after: Harness the chariot to the team, inhabitant of Lachish! She was the beginning of sin for daughter Zion, for Israel’s rebellions were found in you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Harness the chariot to the swift steeds, inhabitant of Lachish. She was the beginning of sin to the daughter of Zion, for in you were found the transgressions of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains parting-gift and false-town wordplay rather than translating names away.
verses.before: So you will give parting gifts to Moresheth-gath. The houses of Achzib will prove deceptive to the kings of Israel.
verses.after: So you will give parting gifts to Moresheth-gath. The houses of Achzib will be a deception to the kings of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore you shall give parting gifts to Moresheth-gath. The houses of Achzib shall prove deceptive to the kings of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps possessor/Mareshah pun and unexplained glory destination.
verses.before: I will again bring a conqueror to you, inhabitant of Mareshah. The glory of Israel will come to Adullam.
verses.after: I will again bring a conqueror to you, inhabitant of Mareshah. Israel’s glory will come to Adullam.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will again bring a conqueror to you, inhabitant of Mareshah. The glory of Israel shall come to Adullam.

verses.rationale: Uses vulture for baldness context within nesher range and preserves bereavement/exile cause.
verses.before: Make yourselves bald and cut off your hair for the children of your delight. Make your baldness as broad as the eagle, for they will go from you into exile.
verses.after: Shave your head and cut off your hair for the children you cherish. Make your baldness wide as a vulture’s, for they have gone into exile away from you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Make yourselves bald and cut off your hair for the children of your delight. Make your baldness as broad as the eagle, for they shall go from you into exile.

verses.rationale: Preserves night planning/morning execution and power rather than mere opportunity.
verses.before: Woe to people who devise wickedness and work out evil upon their beds. When the morning light comes, they carry it out, because it is in the power of their hand.
verses.after: Woe to those who plan wickedness and devise evil on their beds! At morning light they carry it out because the power lies in their hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to those who devise wickedness and work out evil upon their beds. When the morning light comes, they carry it out, because it is in the power of their hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired land/house seizures and family inheritance rather than generic greed.
verses.before: They covet fields and seize them, and houses and take them away. They oppress a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.
verses.after: They covet fields and seize them, houses and take them away. They oppress a man and his household, a person and his inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: They covet fields and seize them, and houses and take them away. They oppress a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.

verses.rationale: Makes the neck image intelligible with yoke while preserving planning's reversal.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD: “Look, I am devising against this family a disaster from which you cannot remove your necks. You will not walk proudly, for it will be a time of calamity.
verses.after: So this is what the LORD says: “I am planning disaster against this family, a yoke you cannot remove from your necks. You will no longer walk proudly, for it will be an evil time.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD: “Behold, I am devising against this family a disaster from which you cannot remove your necks. You shall not walk proudly, for it will be a time of calamity.

verses.rationale: Keeps the lament's pronoun shifts and difficult renegade rather than silently naming invaders.
verses.before: On that day they will take up a taunt against you and lament with bitter lamentation, saying, ‘We are utterly ruined. He changes the portion of my people. How he removes it from me. To the faithless he apportions our fields.’”
verses.after: On that day people will take up a taunt over you and sing a bitter lament: ‘We are utterly devastated! He exchanges my people’s portion. How he takes it from me! He parcels out our fields to a renegade.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day they shall take up a taunt against you and lament with bitter lamentation, saying, ‘We are utterly ruined. He changes the portion of my people. How he removes it from me. To the faithless he apportions our fields.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves land-allotment mechanism and communal exclusion.
verses.before: So you will have no one to cast the measuring line by lot in the assembly of the LORD.
verses.after: So you will have no one to stretch a measuring line for an allotted share in the LORD’s assembly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore you shall have no one to cast the measuring line by lot in the assembly of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains speech's dripping metaphor and marks a plausible opponent quotation while noting uncertain speaker boundaries.
verses.before: “Do not preach,” they preach. “One should not preach of such things. Disgrace will not overtake us.”
verses.after: “Do not pour out such words!” they pour out. “They must not speak about these things; disgrace will not overtake us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Do not preach,” they preach. “One should not preach of such things. Disgrace will not overtake us.”

verses.rationale: Separates objection and divine response while keeping spirit/patience sense explicit in note.
verses.before: Should this be said, O house of Jacob? Has the Spirit of the LORD become impatient? Are these his deeds? Do not my words do good to the one who walks uprightly?
verses.after: Should the house of Jacob say, “Has the LORD’s patience run short? Are these his deeds?” “Do not my words do good to the one who walks uprightly?
verses.tsw_comparator: Should this be said, O house of Jacob? Has the Spirit of the LORD become impatient? Are these his deeds? Do not my words do good to the one who walks uprightly?

verses.rationale: Follows the difficult garment layering and returned-war reading, without substituting peaceful civilians exclusively.
verses.before: But lately my people have risen up as an enemy. You strip the robe from the garment from people who pass by trustingly, returning from war.
verses.after: But lately my people have risen like an enemy. You strip the fine cloak off the garment of those who pass by unsuspecting, returning from war.
verses.tsw_comparator: But lately my people have risen up as an enemy. You strip the robe from the garment from those who pass by trustingly, returning from war.

verses.rationale: Preserves female victims, children, and divine splendor rather than generalizing displacement.
verses.before: The women of my people you drive out from their pleasant houses. From their young children you take away my glory forever.
verses.after: You drive the women of my people from the homes they cherish; you take my splendor from their young children forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: The women of my people you drive out from their pleasant houses. From their young children you take away my glory forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult causal uncleanness and repeated ruin.
verses.before: Arise and go, for this is no place of rest, because it is defiled; it is ruined with a grievous destruction.
verses.after: Get up and go! This is no resting place. Because it is unclean, it brings destruction— grievous destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Arise and go, for this is no place of rest, because it is defiled; it is ruined with a grievous destruction.

verses.rationale: Retains wind/falsehood and ironic welcome for alcohol-promising prophecy.
verses.before: If a man should go about with wind and falsehood, saying, “I will preach to you of wine and strong drink,” he would be the preacher for this people.
verses.after: If someone trafficking in wind and falsehood lied, ‘I will pour out words for you about wine and strong drink,’ he would be the preacher for this people!
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man should go about with wind and falsehood, saying, “I will preach to you of wine and strong drink,” he would be the preacher for this people.

verses.rationale: Retains emphatic gathering and flock noise; enclosure versus Bozrah noted.
verses.before: I will surely gather all of you, O Jacob. I will surely assemble the remnant of Israel. I will set them together like sheep in a fold, like a flock in its pasture. They will be noisy with the multitude of people.
verses.after: I will surely gather all of you, Jacob; I will surely assemble Israel’s remnant. I will bring them together like sheep in an enclosure, like a flock in its pasture, a noisy throng of people.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will surely gather all of you, O Jacob. I will surely assemble the remnant of Israel. I will set them together like sheep in a fold, like a flock in its pasture. They shall be noisy with the multitude of people.

verses.rationale: Keeps breakthrough repetitions and king/LORD relationship without supplying an identity beyond the text.
verses.before: The one who breaks through goes up before them. They break through and pass through the gate and go out by it. Their king passes on before them, the LORD at their head.
verses.after: The one who breaks through goes up before them. They break through, pass the gate, and go out through it. Their king passes before them, with the LORD at their head.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who breaks through goes up before them. They break through and pass through the gate and go out by it. Their king passes on before them, the LORD at their head.

verses.rationale: Preserves prophetic first-person opening and leaders' responsibility to know justice.
verses.before: I said, “Hear now, heads of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel: Is it not for you to know justice?
verses.after: I said: “Listen, heads of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel! Should you not know justice?
verses.tsw_comparator: And I said, “Hear now, heads of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel: Is it not for you to know justice?

verses.rationale: Makes the victims clear from next verse while retaining the graphic butchery metaphor.
verses.before: You who hate good and love evil, who tear the skin from off my people and their flesh from off their bones,
verses.after: You hate good and love evil. You tear the skin from my people and the flesh from their bones.
verses.tsw_comparator: You who hate good and love evil, who tear the skin from off my people and their flesh from off their bones,

verses.rationale: Preserves every violent action rather than paraphrasing exploitation.
verses.before: who eat the flesh of my people, strip their skin from them, break their bones, and chop them up like meat in a pot, like flesh in a cauldron.”
verses.after: You eat my people’s flesh, strip off their skin, break their bones, and chop them up like meat for a pot, like flesh in a cauldron.”
verses.tsw_comparator: who eat the flesh of my people, strip their skin from them, break their bones, and chop them up like meat in a pot, like flesh in a cauldron.”

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal nonresponse and hidden face with stated cause.
verses.before: Then they will cry out to the LORD, but he will not answer them. He will hide his face from them at that time, because they have made their deeds evil.
verses.after: Then they will cry to the LORD, but he will not answer them. He will hide his face from them at that time because their deeds have been evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they will cry out to the LORD, but he will not answer them. He will hide his face from them at that time, because they have made their deeds evil.

verses.rationale: Retains mouth/teeth economy and the contrast of peace versus consecrated war.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD concerning the prophets who lead my people astray, who cry, “Peace,” when they have something to eat, but declare war against him who puts nothing into their mouths:
verses.after: This is what the LORD says about the prophets who lead my people astray: “When they have something between their teeth, they proclaim peace; against anyone who puts nothing in their mouths, they consecrate war.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD concerning the prophets who lead my people astray, who cry, “Peace,” when they have something to eat, but declare war against him who puts nothing into their mouths:

verses.rationale: Keeps loss of revelation expressed through four darkness clauses.
verses.before: So it will be night to you, without vision, and darkness to you, without divination. The sun will go down on the prophets, and the day will be dark over them.
verses.after: So night will come upon you without vision, darkness without divination. The sun will set on the prophets; the day will grow dark over them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore it shall be night to you, without vision, and darkness to you, without divination. The sun shall go down on the prophets, and the day shall be dark over them.

verses.rationale: Retains the physical mourning/shame gesture and lack of divine answer.
verses.before: The seers will be put to shame, and the diviners disgraced. They will all cover their lips, for there is no answer from God.
verses.after: The seers will be ashamed and the diviners disgraced. They will all cover their upper lips, for there is no answer from God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The seers shall be put to shame, and the diviners disgraced. They shall all cover their lips, for there is no answer from God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the prophet's contrasting commission and all enabling qualities.
verses.before: But as for me, I am filled with power, with the Spirit of the LORD, and with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin.
verses.after: But I am filled with power, with the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and courage, to declare Jacob’s rebellion to him and Israel’s sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for me, I am filled with power, with the Spirit of the LORD, and with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin.

verses.rationale: Repeats the leadership summons and straight/crooked contrast.
verses.before: Hear this, you heads of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, who detest justice and make crooked all that is straight,
verses.after: Hear this, heads of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, you who detest justice and twist everything that is straight,
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear this, you heads of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, who detest justice and make crooked all that is straight,

verses.rationale: Keeps the city-building accusation and synonymous place pairing.
verses.before: who build Zion with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity.
verses.after: who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustice.
verses.tsw_comparator: who build Zion with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three corrupt roles and the claim of immunity as their speech.
verses.before: Her heads give judgment for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, and her prophets practice divination for money. Yet they lean upon the LORD and say, “Is not the LORD among us? No disaster will come upon us.”
verses.after: Her heads judge for bribes, her priests teach for a price, and her prophets divine for silver. Yet they lean on the LORD and say, “Is not the LORD among us? No disaster will reach us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Her heads give judgment for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, and her prophets practice divination for money. Yet they lean upon the LORD and say, “Is not the LORD among us? No disaster shall come upon us.”

verses.rationale: Keeps direct responsibility and all three landscape reversals before chapter4's restoration.
verses.before: So because of you Zion will be plowed as a field. Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins, and the mountain of the house a wooded height.
verses.after: So because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become heaps of rubble, and the temple mountain wooded heights.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore because of you Zion shall be plowed as a field. Jerusalem shall become a heap of ruins, and the mountain of the house a wooded height.

verses.rationale: Preserves future mountain elevation and upward-streaming image.
verses.before: It will come to pass in the latter days that the mountain of the house of the LORD will be established as the highest of the mountains, and it will be lifted up above the hills, and peoples will flow to it.
verses.after: In the days to come, the mountain of the LORD’s house will stand established above the mountains, raised higher than the hills. Peoples will stream toward it.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall come to pass in the latter days that the mountain of the house of the LORD shall be established as the highest of the mountains, and it shall be lifted up above the hills, and peoples shall flow to it.

verses.rationale: Keeps nations' active invitation, teaching/walking, and both divine-name occurrences.
verses.before: And many nations will come and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, that he may teach us his ways and that we may walk in his paths.” For out of Zion will go forth instruction, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
verses.after: Many nations will come and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of Jacob’s God. He will teach us his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For instruction will go out from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: And many nations shall come and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, that he may teach us his ways and that we may walk in his paths.” For out of Zion shall go forth instruction, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserves the range of nations and weapon transformations, with exact inverse relation to Joel3:10.
verses.before: He will judge between many peoples and will decide disputes for strong nations far away. And they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, neither will they learn war anymore.
verses.after: He will judge between many peoples and settle disputes for powerful nations far away. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not raise a sword against nation, and they will no longer learn war.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall judge between many peoples and shall decide disputes for strong nations far away. And they shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore.

verses.rationale: Retains household agricultural security and divine mouth assurance.
verses.before: But they will sit, each under his vine and under his fig tree, and none will make them afraid, for the mouth of the LORD of Hosts has spoken.
verses.after: Each will sit beneath his own vine and fig tree, with no one to frighten them, for the mouth of the LORD of Armies has spoken.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they shall sit, each under his vine and under his fig tree, and none shall make them afraid, for the mouth of the LORD of Hosts has spoken.

verses.rationale: Keeps the plural nations' present conduct alongside communal resolve without doctrinal expansion.
verses.before: For all the peoples walk, each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.
verses.after: All the peoples walk, each in the name of its god; but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.
verses.tsw_comparator: For all the peoples walk, each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.

verses.rationale: Preserves marginalized groups and direct admission of divine affliction.
verses.before: “On that day,” declares the LORD, “I will gather the lame, and I will assemble the outcast and those whom I have afflicted.
verses.after: “On that day,” declares the LORD, “I will gather the lame and assemble those driven away, those whom I have afflicted.
verses.tsw_comparator: “In that day,” declares the LORD, “I will gather the lame, and I will assemble the outcast and those whom I have afflicted.

verses.rationale: Keeps reversal from weakness to nation and third-person divine name within speech.
verses.before: And the lame I will make a remnant, and the outcast a strong nation. And the LORD will reign over them in Mount Zion from this time forth and forevermore.
verses.after: I will make the lame a remnant and those cast far off a powerful nation. The LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion from now and forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the lame I will make a remnant, and the outcast a strong nation. And the LORD will reign over them in Mount Zion from this time forth and forevermore.

verses.rationale: Retains tower/stronghold and both daughter designations without fixing the site.
verses.before: And you, O tower of the flock, hill of the daughter of Zion, to you it will come, the former dominion will come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.”
verses.after: And you, tower of the flock, stronghold of daughter Zion— to you the former dominion will come, the kingship of daughter Jerusalem.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, O tower of the flock, hill of the daughter of Zion, to you it shall come, the former dominion shall come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.”

verses.rationale: Keeps unanswered questions and labor comparison as the bridge to exile.
verses.before: Now why do you cry aloud? Is there no king in you? Has your counselor perished, that pain has seized you like a woman in labor?
verses.after: Now why do you cry aloud? Have you no king? Has your counselor perished, that pain grips you like a woman in labor?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now why do you cry aloud? Is there no king in you? Has your counselor perished, that pain has seized you like a woman in labor?

verses.rationale: Preserves Babylon and twice there, locating rescue in the place of exile.
verses.before: Writhe and groan, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor, for now you will go out from the city and dwell in the open country. You will go to Babylon. There you will be rescued; there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
verses.after: Writhe and push, daughter Zion, like a woman giving birth. Now you must leave the city, live in the open country, and go as far as Babylon. There you will be rescued; there the LORD will redeem you from your enemies’ hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Writhe and groan, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor, for now you shall go out from the city and dwell in the open country. You shall go to Babylon. There you shall be rescued; there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.

verses.rationale: Keeps enemy words and their predatory gaze.
verses.before: Now many nations are assembled against you, saying, “Let her be defiled, and let our eyes gaze upon Zion.”
verses.after: Now many nations have gathered against you, saying, “Let her be defiled! Let our eyes feast on Zion!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now many nations are assembled against you, saying, “Let her be defiled, and let our eyes gaze upon Zion.”

verses.rationale: Retains their gathering reinterpreted as divine harvest preparation.
verses.before: But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD; they do not understand his plan, that he has gathered them as sheaves to the threshing floor.
verses.after: But they do not know the LORD’s thoughts or understand his counsel: he has gathered them like sheaves to a threshing floor.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD; they do not understand his plan, that he has gathered them as sheaves to the threshing floor.

verses.rationale: Preserves metal animal imagery and pinned first-person I will devote, not silently you.
verses.before: Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron, and I will make your hooves bronze. You will crush many peoples, and devote their gain to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.
verses.after: “Rise and thresh, daughter Zion! I will make your horn iron and your hooves bronze, and you will crush many peoples. I will devote their gain to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron, and I will make your hooves bronze. You shall crush many peoples, and devote their gain to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.

verses.rationale: Retains troop/daughter wordplay and judge/rod humiliation; cutting oneself alternative noted.
verses.before: Now muster your troops, O daughter of troops. A siege is laid against us. With a rod they strike the judge of Israel upon the cheek.
verses.after: Now muster your troops, daughter of troops! A siege is laid against us. With a rod they strike Israel’s judge on the cheek.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now muster your troops, O daughter of troops. A siege is laid against us. With a rod they strike the judge of Israel upon the cheek.

verses.rationale: Preserves smallness, divine for me, and temporal range without settling preexistence versus ancestral origins in text.
verses.before: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, from you will come forth for me one who is to be ruler in Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient days.
verses.after: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, small among Judah’s clans, from you will come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel, whose origins are from long ago, from ancient days.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to be ruler in Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient days.

verses.rationale: Keeps unnamed he and mother, and male kinship brothers without inserting later identities.
verses.before: So he will give them up until the time when she who is in labor has given birth. Then the rest of his brothers will return to the people of Israel.
verses.after: So he will give them up until the woman in labor has given birth. Then the rest of his brothers will return to the people of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore he shall give them up until the time when she who is in labor has given birth. Then the rest of his brothers shall return to the people of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains two name occurrences, shepherd ruler, and expanded reach.
verses.before: And he will stand and shepherd his flock in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God. And they will dwell secure, for now he will be great to the ends of the earth.
verses.after: He will stand and shepherd in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God. They will dwell securely, for now he will be great to the ends of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he shall stand and shepherd his flock in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God. And they shall dwell secure, for now he shall be great to the ends of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps peace as predicate and seven/eight escalation rather than exact roster speculation.
verses.before: And he will be their peace.
verses.after: And he will be peace. When Assyria enters our land and treads through our citadels, we will raise against him seven shepherds, eight leaders of men.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he shall be their peace.

verses.rationale: Preserves pointed entrances, sword shepherding, and plural-to-singular agency.
verses.before: They will shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod at its entrances. And he will deliver us from the Assyrian when he comes into our land and treads within our border.
verses.after: They will shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword, the land of Nimrod at its entrances. He will rescue us from Assyria when it enters our land and treads within our borders.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod at its entrances. And he shall deliver us from the Assyrian when he comes into our land and treads within our border.

verses.rationale: Keeps the dew's independence and the remnant's position among peoples.
verses.before: Then the remnant of Jacob will be among many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers upon the grass, which do not wait for man nor delay for the children of men.
verses.after: Then Jacob’s remnant among many peoples will be like dew from the LORD, like showers on grass, which do not wait for a person or depend on human beings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers upon the grass, which do not wait for man nor delay for the children of men.

verses.rationale: Retains the severe predator counterpart to the preceding dew image.
verses.before: And the remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, among many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among the flocks of sheep, which, when it passes through, treads down and tears in pieces, and there is none to deliver.
verses.after: Jacob’s remnant among the nations, among many peoples, will be like a lion among forest animals, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which passes through, tramples, and tears, with no one to rescue.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among the flocks of sheep, which, when it passes through, treads down and tears in pieces, and there is none to deliver.

verses.rationale: Keeps lifted-hand victory and complete stated enemy loss.
verses.before: Your hand will be lifted up over your adversaries, and all your enemies will be cut off.
verses.after: Your hand will rise over your adversaries, and all your enemies will be cut off.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your hand shall be lifted up over your adversaries, and all your enemies shall be cut off.

verses.rationale: Preserves removal of the addressed people's military means, not merely enemy weapons.
verses.before: “And on that day,” declares the LORD, “I will cut off your horses from among you and destroy your chariots.
verses.after: “On that day,” declares the LORD, “I will cut off your horses from among you and destroy your chariots.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And in that day,” declares the LORD, “I will cut off your horses from among you and destroy your chariots.

verses.rationale: Retains both cities and fortresses rather than making one explanatory of the other.
verses.before: I will cut off the cities of your land and throw down all your strongholds.
verses.after: I will cut off the cities of your land and tear down all your fortresses.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will cut off the cities of your land and throw down all your strongholds.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated cut-off and distinction practice/practitioner.
verses.before: I will cut off sorceries from your hand, and you will have no more fortune-tellers.
verses.after: I will cut off sorceries from your hands, and you will have no more fortune-tellers.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will cut off sorceries from your hand, and you shall have no more fortune-tellers.

verses.rationale: Retains both objects and handmade-worship critique.
verses.before: I will cut off your carved images and your sacred pillars from among you, and you will no longer bow down to the work of your hands.
verses.after: I will cut off your carved images and sacred pillars from among you. You will no longer bow down to the work of your hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will cut off your carved images and your sacred pillars from among you, and you shall no longer bow down to the work of your hands.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned cities rather than emending to idols and retains named cult objects.
verses.before: I will uproot your Asherah poles from among you and destroy your cities.
verses.after: I will uproot your Asherah poles from among you and destroy your cities.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will uproot your Asherah poles from among you and destroy your cities.

verses.rationale: Keeps the concluding shift to nations and refusal to listen without adding a specified command.
verses.before: And in anger and wrath I will execute vengeance upon the nations that did not obey.”
verses.after: In anger and fury I will take vengeance on the nations that have not listened.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And in anger and wrath I will execute vengeance upon the nations that did not obey.”

verses.rationale: Preserves legal speech and mountains as hearing witnesses.
verses.before: Hear what the LORD says: Rise—plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
verses.after: Hear what the LORD says: “Rise, present your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear what the LORD says: Rise—plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.

verses.rationale: Keeps both name occurrences and repeated case to establish courtroom form.
verses.before: Hear, O mountains, the case of the LORD, you enduring foundations of the earth; for the LORD has a dispute with the people and will bring charges against Israel.
verses.after: Hear the LORD’s case, mountains, you enduring foundations of the earth! The LORD has a case against his people; he will dispute with Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear, O mountains, the case of the LORD, you enduring foundations of the earth; for the LORD has a dispute with the people and will bring charges against Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains intimate address and open questions rather than supplying a charge.
verses.before: O my people, what have I done to you? How have I wearied you? Answer me.
verses.after: “My people, what have I done to you? How have I wearied you? Answer me!
verses.tsw_comparator: O my people, what have I done to you? How have I wearied you? Answer me.

verses.rationale: Preserves slavery, redemption, and all three named leaders including Miriam.
verses.before: For I brought you up from the land of slavery, and redeemed you from the house of oppression; I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
verses.after: I brought you up from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam ahead of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I brought you up from the land of slavery, and redeemed you from the house of oppression; I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.

verses.rationale: Supplies remember journey for the elliptical place pair while retaining all names and righteousness language.
verses.before: O my people, remember now what King Balak of Moab planned, and how Balaam son of Beor answered him, and what happened from Shittim to Gilgal, so that you may remember the saving acts of the LORD.
verses.after: My people, remember what Balak king of Moab planned and what Balaam son of Beor answered him. Remember the journey from Shittim to Gilgal, so you may know the LORD’s righteous acts.”
verses.tsw_comparator: O my people, remember now what King Balak of Moab planned, and how Balaam son of Beor answered him, and what happened from Shittim to Gilgal, so that you may remember the saving acts of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Marks the responding questioner's voice and keeps exact age and offering type.
verses.before: With what will I come before the LORD, and bow myself before the God of all heights? Will I come with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
verses.after: With what shall I approach the LORD and bow before God on high? Shall I approach him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
verses.tsw_comparator: With what shall I come before the LORD, and bow myself before the God of all heights? Shall I come with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?

verses.rationale: Preserves extravagant quantities and disturbing child-sacrifice question as a question, not instruction.
verses.before: Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Will I give my firstborn for my wrongdoing, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
verses.after: Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with tens of thousands of rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my rebellion, the fruit of my body for the sin of my life?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my wrongdoing, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?

verses.rationale: Keeps universal adam, hesed's loyal kindness, and three distinct actions without doctrinal expansion.
verses.before: God has told you, O people, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, to love faithful kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
verses.after: He has told you, human being, what is good. What does the LORD ask of you but to do justice, love faithful kindness, and walk humbly with your God?
verses.tsw_comparator: God has told you, O people, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, to love faithful kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?

verses.rationale: Follows pinned sees/name rather than silently emending to fear/name; flags this very difficult line.
verses.before: The voice of the LORD cries out to the city (it is wisdom to fear your name): Hear, O tribe and assembly of the city!
verses.after: The voice of the LORD calls to the city— wisdom sees your name: “Hear the rod and the one who appointed it!
verses.tsw_comparator: The voice of the LORD cries out to the city (it is wisdom to fear your name): Hear, O tribe and assembly of the city!

verses.rationale: Keeps economic specificity and uncertain opening syntax as a question.
verses.before: Are there still treasures gained by injustice in the house of the wicked, and the dishonest measure that I abhor?
verses.after: Are there still treasures gained by wickedness in the wicked house, and the accursed, undersized ephah?
verses.tsw_comparator: Are there still treasures gained by injustice in the house of the wicked, and the dishonest measure that I abhor?

verses.rationale: Preserves first-person pure wording rather than silently changing to acquit someone else.
verses.before: Can I tolerate wicked scales and a bag of deceitful weights?
verses.after: Can I be pure with wicked scales and a pouch of fraudulent weights?
verses.tsw_comparator: Can I tolerate wicked scales and a bag of deceitful weights?

verses.rationale: Keeps violence and deceit as separate charges and city personification.
verses.before: Your wealthy are full of violence; your inhabitants speak lies, and their tongues are deceitful in their mouths.
verses.after: The city’s rich are full of violence; her inhabitants speak lies, and deceit is on their tongues.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your wealthy are full of violence; your inhabitants speak lies, and their tongues are deceitful in their mouths.

verses.rationale: Preserves disease/striking sense rather than silently repointing to began.
verses.before: So I have begun to strike you, to lay you waste because of your sins.
verses.after: So I too have made you sick with my blows, devastating you because of your sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I have begun to strike you, to lay you waste because of your sins.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult inward lack and frustrated preservation with concrete sword outcome.
verses.before: You will eat but not be satisfied, and emptiness will remain within you; you will put things aside but not preserve them, and what you preserve I will give to the sword.
verses.after: You will eat but not be satisfied; emptiness will remain within you. You will put things away but not save them; what you do save I will give to the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall eat but not be satisfied, and emptiness shall remain within you; you shall put things aside but not preserve them, and what you preserve I will give to the sword.

verses.rationale: Preserves three labor/enjoyment reversals with olive and grape processing.
verses.before: You will sow but not reap; you will tread olives but not anoint yourselves with oil; you will tread grapes but not drink wine.
verses.after: You will sow but not reap; you will tread olives but not anoint yourself with oil, tread grapes but not drink wine.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall sow but not reap; you shall tread olives but not anoint yourselves with oil; you shall tread grapes but not drink wine.

verses.rationale: Retains both dynastic names and pinned my people rather than nations alternative.
verses.before: For you have kept the statutes of Omri, and all the practices of the house of Ahab; you have followed their counsel. Therefore I will make you a desolation, and your inhabitants an object of scorn; you will bear the disgrace of my people.
verses.after: You have kept Omri’s decrees and all the practices of Ahab’s house; you have walked in their counsels. So I will make you a desolation, your inhabitants an object of hissing, and you will bear my people’s disgrace.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have kept the statutes of Omri, and all the practices of the house of Ahab; you have followed their counsel. Therefore I will make you a desolation, and your inhabitants an object of scorn; you shall bear the disgrace of my people.

verses.rationale: Makes the harvest-afterward comparison natural while retaining both missing fruits.
verses.before: Woe is me! For I have become as when the summer fruit has been gathered, as when the grapes have been gleaned: there is no cluster to eat, no first-ripe fig that my soul desires.
verses.after: Woe is me! I am like someone after the summer fruit has been gathered, after the vineyard has been gleaned: no cluster to eat, none of the first-ripe figs I crave.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe is me! For I have become as when the summer fruit has been gathered, as when the grapes have been gleaned: there is no cluster to eat, no first-ripe fig that my soul desires.

verses.rationale: Preserves sweeping lament, fraternal predation, and blood/net imagery.
verses.before: The faithful have perished from the land, and there is no upright person among mankind. They all lie in wait for blood, and each hunts his brother with a net.
verses.after: The faithful have vanished from the land; no upright person remains among humanity. All lie in wait for blood; each hunts his brother with a net.
verses.tsw_comparator: The faithful have perished from the land, and there is no upright person among mankind. They all lie in wait for blood, and each hunts his brother with a net.

verses.rationale: Keeps three corrupt participants and weaving metaphor rather than generic corruption.
verses.before: Their hands are skilled in doing evil. The ruler asks, and the judge takes a bribe, and the great man speaks the desire of his soul, and together they weave it.
verses.after: Their hands are skilled at evil. The ruler demands, the judge takes payment, and the great man declares his own desire; together they weave it into a scheme.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their hands are skilled in doing evil. The ruler asks, and the judge takes a bribe, and the great man speaks the desire of his soul, and together they weave it.

verses.rationale: Retains thorn comparison and source pronoun shifts in the day announcement.
verses.before: The best of them is like a brier, the most upright of them worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen, of your punishment, has come. Now will be their confusion.
verses.after: The best of them is like a brier, the most upright worse than a thorn hedge. The day your watchmen announced, your reckoning, has come. Now comes their confusion.
verses.tsw_comparator: The best of them is like a brier, the most upright of them worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen, of your punishment, has come. Now shall be their confusion.

verses.rationale: Preserves intimate female relationship and mouth-door image in the social-collapse lament.
verses.before: Put no trust in a neighbor; have no confidence in a friend. Guard the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your arms.
verses.after: Do not trust a neighbor or put confidence in a friend. Guard the doors of your mouth even from the woman who lies in your embrace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Put no trust in a neighbor; have no confidence in a friend. Guard the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your arms.

verses.rationale: Keeps every gendered kinship pair and the closing household generalization.
verses.before: For son treats father with contempt, daughter rises against her mother, daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are the men of his own house.
verses.after: A son treats his father with contempt; a daughter rises against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A person’s enemies are the members of his own household.
verses.tsw_comparator: For son treats father with contempt, daughter rises against her mother, daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are the men of his own house.

verses.rationale: Retains watch/wait/hear progression and first-person resolve.
verses.before: But as for me, I will look to the LORD. I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
verses.after: But I will watch for the LORD; I will wait for the God who saves me. My God will hear me.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for me, I will look to the LORD. I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the feminine enemy context in notes and the fall/rise dark/light pairs.
verses.before: Rejoice not over me, my enemy. Though I have fallen, I will rise. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be a light to me.
verses.after: Do not rejoice over me, my enemy. Though I have fallen, I will rise. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rejoice not over me, my enemy. Though I have fallen, I shall rise. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be a light to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps confession alongside hope for legal vindication, without erasing either.
verses.before: I will bear the indignation of the LORD because I have sinned against him, until he pleads my cause and executes justice for me. He will bring me out into the light. I will look upon his righteousness.
verses.after: I will bear the LORD’s indignation because I have sinned against him, until he pleads my case and secures justice for me. He will bring me into the light; I will see his righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bear the indignation of the LORD because I have sinned against him, until he pleads my cause and executes justice for me. He will bring me out into the light. I shall look upon his righteousness.

verses.rationale: Preserves female enemy, quoted taunt, and violent reversal.
verses.before: Then my enemy will see, and shame will cover her who said to me, “Where is the LORD your God?” My eyes will look upon her. Now she will be trampled down like mud in the streets.
verses.after: My enemy will see, and shame will cover her, she who said to me, ‘Where is the LORD your God?’ My eyes will look upon her; now she will be trampled like mud in the streets.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then my enemy will see, and shame will cover her who said to me, “Where is the LORD your God?” My eyes will look upon her. Now she will be trampled down like mud in the streets.

verses.rationale: Chooses boundary for hoq while noting decree alternative; retains promise's terse form.
verses.before: A day for building your walls! On that day the boundary will be far extended.
verses.after: A day for rebuilding your walls! On that day the boundary will be pushed far out.
verses.tsw_comparator: A day for building your walls! In that day the boundary shall be far extended.

verses.rationale: Uses Egypt for Matsor with fortified-cities alternative noted; keeps unnamed River.
verses.before: On that day they will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, from Egypt to the River, from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
verses.after: On that day people will come to you from Assyria and Egypt’s cities, from Egypt to the River, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day they shall come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, from Egypt to the River, from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.

verses.rationale: Retains the counterpoint of judgment beside restoration and fruit metaphor.
verses.before: But the earth will be desolate because of its inhabitants, for the fruit of their deeds.
verses.after: Yet the earth will become desolate because of its inhabitants, as the fruit of their deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the earth shall be desolate because of its inhabitants, for the fruit of their deeds.

verses.rationale: Keeps pastoral petition, solitary woodland setting, and both fertile regions.
verses.before: Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock of your inheritance, who dwell alone in a forest among a fruitful land. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.
verses.after: Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock that is your inheritance, living alone in woodland amid fruitful land. Let them pasture in Bashan and Gilead as in ancient days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock of your inheritance, who dwell alone in a forest in the midst of a fruitful land. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult you/him shift rather than silently normalizing the pronouns.
verses.before: “As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt, I will show them marvelous things.”
verses.after: “As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt, I will show them marvelous things.”

verses.rationale: Keeps humbled military strength and bodily speech/hearing responses.
verses.before: The nations will see and be ashamed of all their might. They will lay their hands on their mouths; their ears will be deaf.
verses.after: Nations will see and be ashamed despite all their might. They will put a hand over their mouths; their ears will become deaf.
verses.tsw_comparator: The nations shall see and be ashamed of all their might. They shall lay their hands on their mouths; their ears shall be deaf.

verses.rationale: Preserves snake/dust abasement and shift to divine direct address.
verses.before: They will lick the dust like a serpent, like crawling things of the earth. They will come trembling from their strongholds. They will turn in fear to the LORD our God, and they will stand in awe of you.
verses.after: They will lick dust like a snake; like creatures crawling on the ground, they will come trembling from their strongholds. They will turn in dread to the LORD our God and be afraid of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall lick the dust like a serpent, like crawling things of the earth. They shall come trembling from their strongholds. They shall turn in fear to the LORD our God, and they shall stand in awe of you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the name-echo question and you/his/he shifts with the remnant qualification.
verses.before: Who is a God like you, forgiving iniquity and passing over transgression for the remnant of his inheritance? He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in steadfast love.
verses.after: Who is a God like you, forgiving guilt and passing over rebellion for the remnant of his inheritance? He does not hold on to anger forever, because he delights in faithful love.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is a God like you, forgiving iniquity and passing over transgression for the remnant of his inheritance? He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in steadfast love.

verses.rationale: Preserves pinned our/their shift and concrete trampling and throwing images.
verses.before: He will again have compassion upon us. He will tread our iniquities underfoot. You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
verses.after: He will again have compassion on us; he will trample our guilt underfoot. You will throw all their sins into the depths of the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will again have compassion upon us. He will tread our iniquities underfoot. You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired ancestors and distinct emet/hesed terms, linking conclusion to enduring oath.
verses.before: You will show faithfulness to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham, as you swore to our fathers from the days of old.
verses.after: You will show faithfulness to Jacob and faithful love to Abraham, as you swore to our ancestors in days long ago.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will show faithfulness to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham, as you swore to our fathers from the days of old.

comparative_references.scope: All 105 TSW verses bound and compared programmatically after independent drafting from each selected original-language record and all annotations. Selected differences read during focused authoring checks. Overlap is triage only.
